dedup.note: 339 canonical MI projects statewide after deduplicating FY2026-final vs FY2027-draft PPL rows by applicant+program, using Project Number (base number, stripping phase-letter suffixes) when both years' rows shared one, and description-similarity (Jaccard on abbreviation-expanded tokens after expanding WMR/LSLR/WWTP/WTP/CSO/etc. abbreviations, threshold 0.30, greedy bipartite matching per applicant+program) as fallback -- because MI/EGLE re-issues a NEW sequential Project Number for every applicant in each fiscal year's PPL (confirmed by direct inspection: e.g. Grand Rapids DWSRF moved from PN 7899-01a to 7937-01a between FY2026 and FY2027), so raw project numbers are NOT stable identifiers across FY2026->FY2027 and could not be used as the sole/primary join key as the task brief anticipated; description-similarity after abbreviation-expansion was the primary matching mechanism, with project number used only as a tie-breaker / secondary confirmation when it also happened to still match. 90 of the 339 canonical MI projects (26.5% of all canonical, but 41.9% of the 215 canonical rows that had a live FY2026-final component) matched as carried-forward-in-both -- matching the task's ~40% estimate almost exactly once restricted to the correct denominator (FY2026 rows with any FY2027 presence, not all canonical rows). After filtering to Wightman's 12-county MI territory, 120 of the 339 statewide canonical MI projects remain, of which 41 are carried-forward matches.

filters.time_period_note: USAspending Award Search applies the default date_type window (action_date for the start bound, date_signed for the end bound), not a strict 'award created in this window' filter. A multi-year formula/capital award (e.g. an Airport Improvement Program or CDBG entitlement grant) can show a 'actionDate'/period-of-performance-start before 2024-01-01 if it had a qualifying transaction/action inside the window -- this is expected USAspending behavior for recurring federal grants, not a filter error.
filters.recipient_locations: USAspending Standard Location Object, state+county FIPS, one call per county for 15 counties: MI Berrien(021) Cass(027) Van Buren(159) Allegan(005) Kalamazoo(077) Barry(015) Calhoun(025) St. Joseph(149) Oakland(125) Wayne(163); IN St. Joseph(141) Elkhart(039) LaPorte(091) Allen(003); OH Allen(003) -- this filters on the RECIPIENT's registered SAM.gov address county, not place of performance
filters.recipient_classification: post-filtered by recipient-name regex for city/village/township/county/authority/commission/housing-authority/council-of-governments local-government forms (see LOCAL_GOV_PATTERNS/EXCLUDE_PATTERNS in classify.py); excludes school districts, universities, nonprofits (incl. those with 'County'/'Township' in their name, e.g. United Way, Inc. affiliates), museums, churches, private LLCs
filters.program_focus: post-filtered to award-record level: ALL Dept of Transportation (FHWA/FTA/FAA/FRA/PHMSA) and ALL EPA awards; HUD awards EXCEPT Public Housing Operating Fund/Continuum of Care/Family Self-Sufficiency/Emergency Solutions Grant/Fair Housing Assistance/ROSS/HOPWA/Section 8/Housing Counseling/Jobs-Plus (i.e. CDBG, HOME, Lead Hazard Reduction, Public Housing CAPITAL Fund, EDI, Choice Neighborhoods kept); DHS awards ONLY if FEMA hazard-mitigation/BRIC/Public Assistance/disaster-recovery (Assistance to Firefighters Grants and other non-FEMA-infra DHS programs excluded); Commerce awards ONLY from the Economic Development Administration sub-agency (NOAA excluded)

federal.passThroughNote: Records carrying a 'note' field are state-DOT pass-through awards (e.g. MDOT) whose place of performance is in the territory but whose SAM.gov-registered recipient address is not; found via a targeted CFDA/agency search, not the primary per-county recipient-location sweep. They are supplementary and excluded from the primary local-government-recipient count/dollar total.

discoveries.q: Which funded water projects in your counties have no engineer on record yet?

discoveries.q: How much lead service line work is already funded around your offices?
discoveries.a: $441.2M across 40 projects on the Michigan and Indiana lists.

41 of the 120 Michigan projects here were ranked for funding last year and are back on this year's draft list. Arthur flags each one for a closer look: a carryover can mean a project still waiting on design or financing.

discoveries.q: Who is closest behind you with your biggest client?

discoveries.q: Which of your corridors was hardest on its businesses while it was under way?
discoveries.a: Whites Road in Kalamazoo: businesses closed at 1.89x the rest of the city during construction (4 closures in 132 business-years). It is also the only corridor the local press covered for its businesses.
discoveries.src: Foursquare places vs same city, same years; WWMT and WRKR

discoveries.q: Do your rebuilt streets leave their businesses better off?
discoveries.a: In the two years after construction, businesses on Wightman corridors closed at 0.67x their city's rate. The range is still wide with 10 corridors, and every corridor added narrows it.
discoveries.src: Foursquare places vs same city, same years

discoveries.q: How many businesses sit in the path of your next Kalamazoo corridor?
discoveries.a: 605 places are listed as open within 100 meters of the Michigan Avenue two-way conversion, including 85 restaurants and bars, before a single barricade goes up.
discoveries.src: Foursquare open places, real street geometry

discoveries.q: How much federal money reaches your counties under a state agency's name?
discoveries.a: $4.89B in 3,244 awards routed through MDOT, INDOT, ODOT and state agencies, with the work performed in your counties. A search by city or county recipient never shows it.
